title: factdiff.revalidate dates a run by the local day and stamps checked_utc in UTC, so test_live_kb fails between local midnight and UTC midnight
goal: factdiff.revalidate's date and its checked_utc stamps name the same day at any hour in any time zone (today() reads the local date, the stamps UTC), so test_live_kb's lookup-eval test passes when the local day is ahead of UTC (found 2026-10-13 00:26 local, 22:26Z, when the whole-suite gate of ST-keicy7gn's landing failed on it after 99 passed)

run: import os,time,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import factdiff;d=[];[(os.environ.__setitem__('TZ',z),time.tzset(),d.append(factdiff.today())) for z in ('Etc/GMT-14','Etc/GMT+12')];print(d);sys.exit(0 if d[0]==d[1] else 1)

gates.question: Which day does factdiff.today() name: the UTC day the checked_utc stamps use, or the local day with the stamps moved to local?

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 12 of 15, "The suite and its gates: faster slow tests, a UTC day, lint that lints, a green selfdoc check and ceiling wordings classed ceiling"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates. Premise run 2026-10-13: the repro prints ['2026-10-14', '2026-10-13'] for TZ Etc/GMT-14 and Etc/GMT+12 and exits 1; factdiff.today() is the local date.
